artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let A be a finite alphabet of "variables" and let Σ be a finite alphabet of letters. A pattern is a word p = p_1 p_2 ... p_n over A. A word w over Σ is said to encounter the pattern p in the abelian sense if w contains a factor of the form u_1 u_2 ... u_n, where each u_i is a non-empty word over Σ, and whenever p_i = p_j the factors u_i and u_j are abelian-equivalent (i.e., u_i is a permutation of u_j; equivalently, u_i and u_j have the same Parikh vector / same multiset of letters). Otherwise, w avoids p in the abelian sense. The pattern p is said to be avoidable in the abelian sense if there exists a finite alphabet Σ and an infinite word w over Σ that avoids p in the abelian sense.

Problem. For each of the following six patterns (written as strings of digits, where each distinct digit denotes a distinct variable), determine whether it is avoidable in the abelian sense:

(1) 01020312,
(2) 01020321,
(3) 01021303,
(4) 01023031,
(5) 010203013,
(6) 010213020.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return any source that resolves the abelian avoidability of the specific six patterns listed. The general literature on abelian pattern avoidance (e.g., classification of short binary/ternary patterns, the result that every binary pattern of length greater than 14 is abelian-2-avoidable) does not appear to settle these particular patterns, which involve 4 or 5 variables. The status is therefore not verifiable from the searches available.
